root_cause.text: In `mana_hwc_destroy_channel()`, `hwc->caller_ctx` was freed before tearing down the Completion Queue (CQ) and Event Queue (EQ), allowing a concurrent interrupt handler (`mana_hwc_rx_event_handler()`) to access freed memory because IRQ synchronization (deregistration) only occurs during CQ/EQ destruction.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves the `kfree(hwc->caller_ctx)` after the `mana_hwc_destroy_cq()` call. The CVE description explicitly states: "mana_smc_teardown_hwc() signals the hardware to stop but does not synchronize against IRQ handlers already executing on other CPUs. The IRQ synchronization only happens in mana_hwc_destroy_cq() via mana_gd_destroy_eq() -> mana_gd_deregister_irq(). Since this runs after kfree(hwc->caller_ctx), a concurrent mana_hwc_rx_event_handler() can dereference freed caller_ctx."

Sets caller_ctx to NULL after freeing it, but does not prevent concurrent access that may have already occurred; part of the flawed freeing sequence.
Conditional that leads to WQ destruction after caller_ctx is freed, but before CQ destruction; the ordering relative to CQ teardown contributes to the window of vulnerability.
Destroys the work queue after caller_ctx is freed, but before CQ and EQ teardown; part of the out-of-order teardown sequence.
Checks for CQ existence after caller_ctx has been freed; this line should come before the free to ensure IRQ handlers are disabled first.

vuln_statements.explanation: Directly frees caller_ctx before CQ/EQ teardown, allowing a concurrent interrupt handler to access freed memory via the callback, leading to use-after-free. This is the primary vulnerable operation.

Sets caller_ctx to NULL after the free, but does not prevent concurrent access that may have already occurred while the pointer was valid. Part of the flawed freeing sequence that does not ensure IRQ handlers are disabled first.

Conditional check for CQ existence placed after caller_ctx is freed. The CQ destruction (which triggers IRQ deregistration/synchronization) should have been performed before freeing caller_ctx to close the race window. This placement contributes to the vulnerable ordering.

Destroys the completion queue, which triggers IRQ deregistration and synchronization. This is placed too late, after caller_ctx is already freed, allowing a concurrent handler to still access the freed memory before the CQ is destroyed.
